signatures: `hasSubscribers` Returns: {boolean} If there are active subscribers
`hasSubscribers` Returns: {boolean} `true` if any of the individual channels has a subscriber, `false` if not.

reason: The bound store must be an AsyncLocalStorage instance (the lowering keys bindings by its handle); Node keys a binding by any value the program passes.

A call to a global console output member, a Console instance's output method, the console object called as a value and a method held as a separate function value publish the call's own argument array on the matching channel before the line is written, when the channel has subscribers; every argument type crosses, including a spread's elements, because node:console's output is util.format over that same array.

Node emits these around each CommonJS require() and ESM import() call from its module loaders. A compiled program resolves statically linked modules at compile time: there is no per-call load at run time to trace, and emitting the events would mean instrumenting every require and import site in the module lowering, with the loader's id and parentFilename context. That is module-loader work, not diagnostics_channel work.
